methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a correct model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the relationship out loud exposes missing links and helps build a usable mental model.
how: State the idea in your own words.
Check your attempt against the model and fix any mismatch.
Explain it again without copying the model.
methodBriefing.completion: You can explain both ideas clearly, including the direction of water movement and why concentration differences matter.

Keep the membrane idea before the osmosis idea.

activities.label: Membrane crossing model
activities.title: How water crosses a membrane
activities.body: Read the model and note the key relationship.

essentialIdeas: A selectively permeable membrane lets some substances cross more easily than others, so water can move across it.

activities.label: Explain membrane movement
activities.title: Explain the membrane idea
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain how water can move across a selectively permeable membrane.
activities.concept: A selectively permeable membrane lets some substances cross more easily than others, so water can move across it.
activities.correctAnswer: Water can move across a selectively permeable membrane because the membrane lets some substances pass more easily than others.
activities.feedback: A complete answer says that the membrane is selective and that water can still cross. A common gap is saying only that the membrane is a barrier.

activities.label: Repair the osmosis rule
activities.title: What drives osmosis
activities.body: Fix your answer using the model and state the direction of water movement.
activities.concept: Osmosis is the net movement of water toward the side with fewer water molecules and more dissolved particles.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves by osmosis toward the side with fewer water molecules and more dissolved particles.
activities.feedback: A complete answer includes both the direction and the concentration difference. A common gap is reversing the direction or leaving out what is different on the two sides.

activities.label: Explain osmosis again
activities.title: Explain osmosis again
activities.body: Now explain osmosis in your own words without copying the model.
activities.concept: Osmosis is the net movement of water toward the side with fewer water molecules and more dissolved particles.
activities.correctAnswer: Osmosis is the net movement of water toward the side with fewer water molecules and more dissolved particles.
activities.feedback: A complete answer connects osmosis to concentration differences and net movement of water. If needed, restate which side has more dissolved particles and which side receives water.

check.referenceAnswer: It allows water to pass across while limiting many other substances.
check.feedback: Good if you link permeability to water passing and not to all substances equally.

items.essentialIdea: Osmosis moves water from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.

check.title: Direction of osmosis
check.prompt: In osmosis, how does water move when concentration differs across a membrane?
check.referenceAnswer: Water moves from the side with more water and fewer dissolved particles to the side with less water and more dissolved particles.
check.feedback: Correct if you include both the water difference and the dissolved-particle difference.

recognitionCheck.title: Osmosis direction
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best describes osmosis across a selectively permeable membrane?
choices: Water moves from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
Dissolved particles move from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
Water moves only when the membrane allows all substances through.
Water moves from lower water concentration to higher water concentration.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: Water moves from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
recognitionCheck.feedback: This matches osmosis; the other choices reverse the direction or shift the substance.
